design: Each art pixel of frame 0 gets a class (the sea's animation never moves the coastline, so frame 0 stands for all): - water: blue over red by more than 15 and over green by at least 15. This keeps the white wave crests (blue still leads) as water, and the sand, foliage, roofs (b <= r) and the grey-blue shade of walls and stone (b about g) as land. - shallows: teal water: green at least 0.62 of blue and 45 over red. The open sea's green is about 0.48 of its blue; the lighter halo the art paints along the shores rises to about 0.8 at the beach, and 0.62 takes its inner half. The halo's green is 55 to 75 over its red, the soft edges of the open sea's wave crests only 25 to 37 (they whiten all three channels), so they stay sea. - sea: the other water; land: everything that is not water. A terrain pixel (640x480) covers 2.25 x 2.25 art pixels at 1080p; it takes the class with the largest covered area, ties going to land, then shallows. Map: pixels sea 29822, shallows 5843, land 29871; tiles all sea 60, all land 57, mixed 139.
